ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r1.claim: «We have taken you as an ill omen» means they regarded the messengers as a bad portent; the speaker reports explanations involving withheld rain or increased leprosy after denial.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r1.anchor: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم: أي تشاء منا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r2.claim: He says rain was withheld from the people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r3.claim: He says the omen most likely reflects division and social discord, like Quraysh’s superstition about Muḥammad and the charge made against Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر أن تطير هؤلاء كان سبب ما دخل فيهم من اختلاف الكلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r4.claim: He explains the superstition psychologically: people call what they desire blessed and what they dislike ill-omened, as in the Qurʾānic accounts of Pharaoh’s people and Meccan polytheists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r4.anchor: وعادة الجهال أن يتمنوا بكل شيء مالوا إليه واشتهوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r5.claim: He paraphrases their accusation as saying that any misfortune they suffer is because of the messengers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة: إن أصابنا شيء كان من أجلكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r6.claim: They threaten to stone the messengers; their promised painful punishment is burning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p53#2/r6.anchor: لنرجمنكم بالحجارة، قاله قتادة. عذاب أليم: هو الحريق

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.claim: The sūrah recalls a town warned by two messengers, then a third helper; its people rejected them, blamed the warning signs, threatened them, and were destroyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p371/r1.anchor: two messengers were sent by God to warn its people

TABRISI:36:11-20/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:11-20/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:11-20/r4.claim: When Shimon sees his words affect the king, he calls him to God; the king and some subjects believe, while others disbelieve.
TABRISI:36:11-20/r4.anchor: فلما علم شمعون أن قوله أثر في الملك دعاه إلى الله فآمن وآمن من أهل مملكته قوم وكفر آخرون.

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r1.claim: The opponents escalate as the messengers intensify their preaching: after rejecting their claim and oath, they answer with another assertion, this time accusing them of ill omen.

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r2.claim: Their superstition treats the messengers as a renewed cause of misfortune, invoking the proverb that a false oath leaves homes desolate.

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r3.claim: “We will stone you” may mean verbally curse or insult you; then “painful punishment” escalates the threat to physical beating and pain.

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, they threaten actual stoning, with the following phrase explaining that they will continue pelting the messengers until death, making the punishment painful.

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r5.claim: One analysis takes alīm as “pain-causing,” with the rare pattern فعيل functioning like مفعل.
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذكرنا في الأليم أنه بمعنى لمؤلم

RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p47#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, alīm means “possessing pain,” with فعيل functioning as فاعل, a common pattern like “an evening that is pleased” in 69:21.

RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.claim: Alternatively, Satan is called rajim because God ordered angels to drive devils from the heavens with meteors; the description then extends to every evil rebel.
RAZI-FULL:v1p61/r6.anchor: أن الشيطان إنما وصف بكونه مرجوما لأنه تعالى أمر الملائكة برمي الشياطين بالشهب والثواقب طردا لهم من السموات

STUDYQURAN:36:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:36:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:36:18/r1.claim: The disbelievers reply to the message bearers that they see an ill omen in them or foretell punishment that will befall them.
STUDYQURAN:36:18/r1.anchor: This is the response of the disbelievers to the message bearers, meaning, “We see an ill omen or foretell a punishment that will befall you.”

BURSEVI:v7p298/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r1.claim: Tatayyur originally meant taking birds flying to the right as auspicious and birds flying left as ominous, then came to mean any object of superstition.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r1.anchor: أصل التطير التفاؤل بالطير فإنهم يزعمون أن الطائر السانح سبب للخير والبارح سبب للشر كما سبق في النمل ثم استعمل في كل ما يتشاءم به

BURSEVI:v7p298/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r2.claim: The townspeople's superstition reflects ignorant people who call whatever suits their desires good even when harmful, and reject what displeases them even when it brings success in both worlds.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r2.anchor: جريا على ديدن الجهلة حيث كانوا يتيمنون بكل ما يوافق شهواتهم وإن كان مستجلبا لكل شر ووبال

BURSEVI:v7p298/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r3.speaker: النقشبندي
BURSEVI:v7p298/r3.claim: Al-Naqshbandi explains their complaint as saying that no rain fell and calamities began after the messengers arrived, so they should leave and stop preaching.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r3.anchor: قال النقشبندي : قد تشاءمنا بقدومكم إذ منذ قدمتم إلى ديارنا ما نزل القطر علينا

BURSEVI:v7p298/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r4.claim: The Prophet liked good omens and disliked superstition: an omen rests on good opinion of God, while superstition relies on something besides Him.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r4.anchor: وكان عليه السلام يحب التفاؤل ويكره التطير والفرق بينهما أن الفأل إنما هو من طريق حسن الظن بالله

BURSEVI:v7p298/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p298/r5.claim: On the way to Medina the Prophet met Burayda ibn Aslam; hearing his name, he told Abu Bakr their affair was eased, and hearing his lineage, said they were safe from their enemies' plot.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r5.anchor: لما توجه النبي عليه السلام نحو المدينة لقي بريدة بن أسلم

BURSEVI:v7p298/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p298/r6.claim: The wordplay was “برد أمرنا وصلح” (“our affair has cooled and gone well”) and “سلمنا من كيدهم” (“we are safe from their plotting”).

BURSEVI:v7p298/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r7.claim: Some jurists say a person commits unbelief by treating an owl's or another bird's cry as predicting a patient's death, or by returning from travel because of a magpie's call.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r7.anchor: وفي الفقه : لو صاحت الهامة أو طير آخر فقال : رجل يموت المريض يكفر

BURSEVI:v7p298/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v7p298/r8.claim: A hadith says that when an omen enters a person's heart, he should affirm his servitude to God and God's power, deny that anything but God brings good or removes evil, then proceed.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "ليس عبد إلا سيدخل في قلبه الطيرة فإذا أحس بذلك فليقل أنا عبد الله

BURSEVI:v7p298/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r10.claim: Their oath means, “By God, if you do not stop this claim and fall silent about us,” with the accompanying Persian gloss saying to desist from their preaching.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r10.anchor: والله لئن لم تمتنعوا عن مقالتكم هذه ولم تسكتوا عنا

BURSEVI:v7p298/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r11.claim: To stone them means to throw stones at them.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r11.anchor: الرجم : سنكسار كردن) أي : لنرمينكم بالحجارة

BURSEVI:v7p298/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p298/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p298/r12.claim: The threat means they will not stop after one or two stones but will continue stoning them to death, or that the stoning itself will inflict painful torment.
BURSEVI:v7p298/r12.anchor: أي : لا نكفي برجمكم بحجر أو حجرين بل نديم ذلك عليكم إلى الموت وهو العذاب الأليم

TAB-FULL:v19p416/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r1.claim: The townspeople say they took the messengers as a bad omen and blame them if misfortune strikes.
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم} [يس: 18] قالوا: «إن أصابنا شر، فإنما هو من أجلكم»

TAB-FULL:v19p416/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r2.claim: Qatada says the threat means: if evil befalls us, it is because of you.
TAB-FULL:v19p416/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم} [يس: 18] قالوا: «إن أصابنا شر، فإنما هو من أجلكم»

TAB-FULL:v19p417/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p417/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p417/r1.claim: The townspeople threaten to stone the messengers if they do not stop claiming to be sent and forbidding worship of the idols.

TAB-FULL:v19p417/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p417/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p417/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the threat as stoning them and inflicting a painful punishment.
TAB-FULL:v19p417/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم} [يس: 18] بالحجارة {وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم} [يس: 18] يقول: «ولينالنكم منا عذاب موجع»

TABATABAI:36:15-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r6.claim: The townspeople address the messengers; تطيرنا means taking them as an ill omen, and the rest is a threat to stone them and inflict painful punishment unless they stop preaching.
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r6.anchor: القائلون أصحاب القرية والمخاطبون هم الرسل، والتطير هو التشأم

TABATABAI:36:15-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r7.claim: They threaten to stone the messengers and bring painful punishment upon them if they do not stop delivering the message and calling people to it.
TABATABAI:36:15-19/r7.anchor: لئن لم تنتهوا عن التبليغ ولم تكفوا عن الدعوة لنرجمنكم بالحجارة وليصلن إليكم وليقعن بكم منا عذاب أليم

TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ relates that Jesus sent two disciples to Antioch; after they healed Habib al-Najjar's ill son, the king interrogated and beat them, and news of their miracles spread.
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r2.anchor: في المجمع قالوا بعث عيسى رسولين من الحواريين إلى مدينة أنطاكية فلما قربا من المدينة رأيا شيخا

TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.claim: Wahb says the messengers never reached the king; he imprisoned and flogged them, so Jesus sent Shimʿun al-Ṣafa undercover. Shimʿun befriended the court, arranged a public test, and the messengers restored sight to a blind youth and raised a seven-day dead man, prompting some to believe.
TABATABAI:36:13-32/r3.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه بعث عيسى هذين الرسولين إلى أنطاكية فأتياها ولم يصلا إلى ملكها

TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.claim: Al-ʿAyyāshī, through al-Thumālī and others, reports a variant in which God sent two messengers and then a third, Jesus sent Shimʿun to rescue them, and the revived dead man was the king's son; the king and his people believed.
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r1.anchor: عن الثمالي وغيره عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام إلا أن في بعض الروايات

TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the king disbelieved and joined his people in resolving to kill the messengers; Habib, at the city's far gate, ran to urge obedience to them.
TABATABAI:36:13-32#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق بل كفر الملك وأجمع هو وقومه على قتل الرسل

TABRISI:36:14/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14/r8.claim: Tataiyarna means that they took the messengers as an ill omen; the word derives from Arabs' use of birds for omens, auspicious or inauspicious.
TABRISI:36:14/r8.anchor: وأصل تطيرنا تفعلنا من الطائر عند العرب الذي به يتشاءمون ويتيمنون

TABRISI:36:14-19/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:36:14-19/r14.claim: The townspeople say they took the messengers as an ill omen.
TABRISI:36:14-19/r14.anchor: أي تشاءمنا بكم { لئن لم تنتهوا } عما تدعونه من الرسالة

TABRISI:36:14-19/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r15.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:36:14-19/r15.claim: Qatada explains their threat as stoning the messengers.

TABRISI:36:14-19/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:36:14-19/r16.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:36:14-19/r16.claim: Mujahid instead explains the threat as insulting the messengers.

THALABI:v8p125/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r11.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p125/r11.claim: Muqatil says rain was withheld, so the people blamed the envoys as an ill omen.
THALABI:v8p125/r11.anchor: قال مقاتل: حبس عنهم المطر فقالوا: هذا بشؤمكم

THALABI:v8p125/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r12.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p125/r12.claim: Qatada says the threat meant pelting the envoys with stones.
THALABI:v8p125/r12.anchor: قال قتادة: بالحجارة، وقال آخرون: لنقتلنكم

THALABI:v8p125/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p125/r13.claim: Other interpreters take the threat as a promise to kill the messengers.
THALABI:v8p125/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: بالحجارة، وقال آخرون: لنقتلنكم

THALABI:v8p125/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p125/r14.claim: The envoys say the people's ill omen lies with them because of disbelief.

THALABI:v8p125/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r15.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v8p125/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak gloss the portent as their share of good and evil.
THALABI:v8p125/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك: حظكم من الخير والشر.

THALABI:v8p125/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r16.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v8p125/r16.claim: Qatada interprets the portent as their deeds.
THALABI:v8p125/r16.anchor: قال قتادة: أعمالكم، وقرأ الحسن والأعرج: طيركم.

THALABI:v8p125/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p125/r17.speaker: الحسن والأعرج
THALABI:v8p125/r17.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Araj read طيركم for طائركم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r1.claim: The people say they took the messengers as a bad omen: rain had stopped, and they blamed the misfortune on them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r1.anchor: فقال القوم للرسل: {إنا تطيرنا بكم} يعني: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك أن المطر حبس عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r2.claim: The threat means: if you do not stop.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r3.claim: Al-Farra says rajm here means killing, as in 11:91, and that most Quranic uses of rajm mean killing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p465#4/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: (كقوله: {ولولا رهطك لرجمناك} [هود: 91] يريد القتل، وعامة الرجم في القرآن القتل)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r1.claim: The people took the messengers as an ill omen because rain had been withheld, and threatened to stone them to death if they did not stop.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r1.anchor: وذلك أنهم حبس عنهم المطر، فقالوا: هذا بشؤمكم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r2.claim: Their threat to stone the messengers means they would kill them by pelting them with stones.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:36:18-22/r2.anchor: لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم } لنقتلنكم رجما بالحجارة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r4.claim: The townspeople say they have taken the messengers as a bad omen.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r4.anchor: قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم} [يس: 15-18] تشاءمنا بكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r5.claim: Qatāda reports that they said any misfortune striking them would be because of the messengers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: قالوا: إن أصابنا سوء فهو من قبلكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r6.speaker: الحسن وغيره
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others take the threat to mean they would kill the messengers; al-Ḥasan specifies stoning them to death.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r6.anchor: لنقتلكم في تفسير الحسن وغيره، غير أن الحسن قال: لنرجمنكم بالحجارة حتى نقتلكم بها

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r7.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r7.claim: Al-Suddī also glosses the threat as killing them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r8.claim: They threaten to inflict painful punishment before killing the messengers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p803#2/r8.anchor: {وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم} [يس: 18] موجع قبل أن نقتلكم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.claim: The town's persistent rejection of three prophets, scorn for a believer who supported them, and likely murder of him is set before the Meccan opponents of Muhammad as a cautionary example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r1.anchor: Kendilerine üç peygamber birden gönderilmesine rağmen inkârcılıkta direnen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r5.claim: The dialogue of verses 14–19 shows the townspeople openly persisting in disbelief with insulting and threatening language.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r5.anchor: şehir halkı, hakaret ve tehditlerle dolu bir üslûp kullanarak inkârcılıkta direneceklerini açıkça ifade etmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.claim: The story warns those who persist in rejecting God's message and opposing His messengers, warns Muhammad's deniers, and strengthens his followers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:13/r21.anchor: bir taraftan Hz. Muhammed’in peygamberliğini inkâr edenlere güçlü bir uyarı yaparken diğer yandan da ona tâbi olanların mâneviyatını yükseltmektir.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.claim: The Yā Sīn narrative, including the messengers’ arrival and the people’s threat, follows an implied question-and-answer pattern; al-Jurjānī says this reading applies throughout the passage.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p186/r1.anchor: التقدير الذي قدرناه من معنى السؤال والجواب بين في ذلك كله

DAMGHANI:v1p196/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r5.claim: Rajm can mean killing; the threatened people say they will kill the messengers.
DAMGHANI:v1p196/r5.anchor: الرجم يعني القتل قوله تعالى في سورة يس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r4.claim: A second sense is killing; Ibn Qutayba says the metaphor arose because people killed by stoning.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p317/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : وإنما استعير الرجم في موضع القتل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r10.claim: In the messengers’ threat, al-ʿadhāb means painful beating or assault.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r10.anchor: والثامن : الضرب المؤلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في يس

FARRA:v2p373#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p373#2/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p373#2/r7.claim: Here rajm means killing; most Quranic uses of rajm likewise mean killing, as in the people of Shuʿayb's threat.
FARRA:v2p373#2/r7.anchor: يريد: لنقتلنكم. وعامة ما كان في القرآن من الرجم فهو قتل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says they meant that any misfortune that struck them was caused by the messengers.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p364#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: يقولون: إن أصابنا شر فهو بكم.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r2.claim: Rajm figuratively means killing because people were killed by stoning; the first murder was reportedly by stones, so the term later applied even without stones.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274/r2.anchor: ثم يستعار فيوضع موضع القتل، لأنهم كانوا يقتلون بالرجم

NAHHAS:v3p387/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p387/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p387/r9.claim: Here the threat means we will kill you; الرجم generally means killing in Qur'anic usage.
NAHHAS:v3p387/r9.anchor: أي لنقتلنكم قال وعامة ما في القرآن من الرجم معناه القتل

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r6.claim: The people say that they regard the messengers as an ill omen.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r6.anchor:
قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم)
أي نشاءمنا

ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r7.claim: The threat means that they will stone the messengers to death.
ZAJJAJ:v4p281#2/r7.anchor:
لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم).
أي لنقتلنكم رجما

ASAD-NOTES:36:18#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:36:18#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:36:18#n12/r1.claim: Asad directs readers to note 95 on surah 7 for the meaning of tatayyarna bikum, translated here as auguring evil from the messengers.
ASAD-NOTES:36:18#n12/r1.anchor: For an explanation of the phrase tat ayyania bikum, see surah 7, note 95.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.claim: The city account warns Quraysh that rejecting God's messengers leads to destruction: the first two are rejected, a third supports them, and the people dismiss signs, blame bad luck, and threaten the messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p377/r4.anchor: The Almighty sent two of His messengers to warn the inhabitants of this city; however, they denied both of them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r3.claim: Here taṭayyarū means to regard someone or something as a bad omen bringing bad luck.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r3.anchor: Here it means to regard something as a bad omen and one that brings bad luck.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r4.claim: Instead of taking Egypt's calamities as warnings about their own deeds, the people blamed Moses and his followers, claiming their message angered the deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r4.anchor: they regarded them be bad omens from Moses (sws) and his followers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r5.claim: They threatened to stone Moses and his companions and cause further harm if they did not stop preaching, ostensibly to protect their deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r5.anchor: they will stone them to death in order to protect their deities.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r6.claim: He links this accusation to 7:130–131: drought and reduced fruit were sent so Pharaoh's people might heed, but they claimed good times for themselves and blamed Moses and his companions for calamity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p386/r6.anchor: This topic is also discussed in Sūrah A‘rāf in the following words

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141/r1.claim: Qatāda explains that the people blamed the messengers for any misfortune, while the messengers replied that their ill omen was with them and arose because they were reminded.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p141/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إنا تطيرنا بكم ﴾ قال يقولون إن أصابنا شر فهو بكم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r1.claim: After their arguments failed, the people called the messengers ill omens, following ignorant habits of favoring what suits desire and fearing what does not, regardless of actual good or harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r1.anchor: لما ضاقت عليهم الحيل وعييت بهم العلل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, they feared the warning of harm if they did not believe, so they recoiled from the call.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r2.anchor: أو بناء على أن الدعوة لا تخلو عن الوعيد بما يكرهونه من إصابة ضر إن لم يؤمنوا

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r3.claim: Muqatil says rain was withheld from the people.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r4.speaker: آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r4.claim: Another report says leprosy spread quickly among them after they rejected the messengers.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r4.anchor: آخر : اسرع فيهم الجذام عند تكذيبهم الرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r5.speaker: إبن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya attributes their superstition to division and discord among the people; the wording indicates the preaching triggered it.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r5.anchor: إبن عطية : أن تطير هؤلاء كان بسبب ما دخل فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r6.claim: Their threat means the messengers must stop making this statement.

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r7.claim: Qatada says the threatened stoning means killing with stones, though it could instead mean harming them by stoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r7.anchor: بالحجارة قاله قتادة وذكر فيه احتمالان إحتمال أن يكون الرجم للقتل

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r8.claim: Mujahid, in a report from Abd ibn Humayd, interprets rajm as cursing or insulting, and says rajm throughout the Qur'an means insult.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : أي لنشتمنكم

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r9.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r9.claim: Al-Bahr glosses the painful punishment as burning; another opinion says it leaves its victims alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r9.anchor: في البحر : وهو الحريق وقيل عذاب غيره تبقى معه الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r10.claim: The threats can mean stoning them to death or excruciating punishment if they survive; alternatively, the threats may be bodily and spiritual, with assignments reversed in another view.
ALUSI-FULL:v22p223#2/r10.anchor: والمراد لنقتلنكم بالحجارة أو لنعذبنكم إذا لم نقتلكم عذابا أليما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r2.claim: The townspeople took the messengers as an ill omen because the rain had stopped, and blamed them for it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r2.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك أن المطر حبس عنهم، فقالوا: أصابنا هذا بشؤمكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r3.claim: Their threat to stone the messengers means they would kill them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r4.claim: Qatada specifically explains the threatened stoning as throwing stones at them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p13/r5.claim: The townspeople threaten to inflict painful punishment on the messengers.

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r7.claim: The people say they take the envoys as an ill omen because the message seems strange, offensive, and repellent to them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r7.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك لاستغرابهم ما ادعوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r8.claim: They threaten to stone the envoys and inflict painful punishment unless they stop their preaching.
BAYDAWI-FULL:36:15-19/r8.anchor: عن مقالتكم هذه. { لنرجمنكم وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r3.claim: The arrival of righteous people among a community can be a blessing or a punishment according to whether people believe and act well; these deniers faced drought, hardship, and other trials.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r3.anchor: حلول الصالحين بين الناس يكون تارة نعمة وأخرى نقمة باعتبار التصديق والتكذيب والإساءة والإحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r4.claim: The townspeople say they deliberately and conspicuously took the messengers as a bad omen, blaming their misfortune on them; this explicit wording differs from expressions in al-Naml and al-Aʿraf.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r4.anchor: أي حملنا أنفسنا على الطيرة والتشاوم تطيرا ظاهرا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r5.claim: The ignorant custom is to call what they favor auspicious and credit its blessings to good fortune, then blame disliked events on the ill omen of others.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r5.anchor: عادة الجهال التيمن بما مالوا إليه ويسندون ما حل بهم من نعمة إلى يمنة والتشاوم بما كرهوه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r6.speaker: أهل القرية
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r6.claim: They demand that the messengers stop their summons, and insist under oath that they will not relent in their threat.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r6.anchor: أي عن دعائكم هذا { لنرجمنكم } أي لنشتمنكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r7.claim: Rajm here may mean cursing or insulting, pelting with stones until they stop, or killing them brutally.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r7.anchor: أي لنشتمنكم أو لنرمينكم بالحجارة حتى تنتهوا أو لنقتلنكم شر قتلة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r8.claim: The threat promises that punishment will come from the townspeople themselves, emphasizing that they will personally inflict it.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r8.anchor: أي عاجلا لا من غيرنا كما تقولون أنتم في تهديدكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r9.claim: He explains the choice of 'touch' over 'contact' by noting that a person may act without the intended effect taking hold.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p251/r9.anchor: ولما كان الإنسان قد يفعل ما لا يؤخذ أثره فقالوا معبرين بالمس دون الإمساس

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r7.claim: Qatada says the townspeople blamed any misfortune on the envoys and threatened to stone them unless they stopped preaching.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم} قال: يقولون إن أصابنا شر فإنما هو من أجلكم {لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم} بالحجارة

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r8.claim: Qatada glosses “your omen is with you” as your deeds are with you, and says “if you are reminded” means they took the reminder of God as an ill omen.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r8.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {قالوا إنا تطيرنا بكم} قال: يقولون إن أصابنا شر فإنما هو من أجلكم {لئن لم تنتهوا لنرجمنكم} بالحجارة {قالوا طائركم معكم} أي أعمالكم معكم

DURR-FULL:v7p50/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r9.claim: Mujahid says the threat “we will stone you” means “we will revile you”; he also says what was decreed for people will come upon them.
DURR-FULL:v7p50/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {لنرجمنكم} قال: لنشتمنكم قال والرجم في القرآن كله الشتم وفي قوله {طائركم معكم أئن ذكرتم} يقول: ما كتب عليكم واقع بكم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3192/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3192/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3192/r1.claim: Qatādah says the people blamed the messengers for any misfortune, threatened to stone and painfully punish them, and were told their omen was their own deeds; they took reminders of God as ill omens.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3192/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله ، عنه في قوله : قالوا انا تطيرنا بكم قال : يقولون ان اصابنا شر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.claim: Some interpreters say leprosy spread quickly among the townspeople when they denied the messengers, prompting their ill omen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض المتأولين: إن أهل هذه القرية أسرع فيهم الجذام عند تكذيبهم المرسلين فلذلك قالوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.claim: Maqatil says rain was withheld from the town, prompting the threat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: احتبس عنهم المطر فلذلك قالوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r3.claim: تطيرنا means we took you as an ill omen; it derives from using birds for divination, a practice widespread among peoples, and the verb usually denotes bad luck although bird omens could be favorable or unfavorable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r3.anchor: ومعناه تشاءمنا بكم، مأخوذ من الحكم بالطير، وهو معنى متداول في الأمم وقلما يستعمل تطيرت إلا في الشؤم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r4.claim: The likeliest cause of their omen was the social division and turmoil in their town, as with Quraysh's omen about Muhammad and the words addressed to Moses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r4.anchor: والأظهر أن تطير هؤلاء إنما كان بسبب ما دخل قريتهم من اختلاف الكلمة وافتتان الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r5.claim: Qatada says they meant that any misfortune to befall them would be because of the messengers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: قالوا إن أصابنا شر فإنما هو من أجلكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p449#2/r6.claim: Qatada explains their threat to stone the messengers as literal stoning with rocks.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r1.claim: The people blamed the messengers for a drought, saying the rain had been withheld because of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r1.anchor: وذلك أن المطر حبس عنهم فقالوا إنما أصابنا هذا من قبلكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r2.claim: The threat's condition means if the messengers do not stop speaking against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p12/r2.anchor: ﴿ لئن لم تنتهوا ﴾ أي تسكتوا عنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r1.claim: The townspeople say the messengers' arrival has brought no good fortune to their lives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r1.anchor: أي: لم نر على وجوهكم خيرا في عيشنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r2.claim: Qatada says they mean that any misfortune striking them is because of the messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: يقولون إن أصابنا شر فإنما هو من أجلكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r3.claim: Mujahid says they claim that whenever people like the messengers entered a town, its inhabitants were punished.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: يقولون: لم يدخل مثلكم إلى قرية إلا عذب أهلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r4.claim: Qatada interprets their threat to stone the messengers literally as pelting them with stones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: بالحجارة. وقال مجاهد: بالشتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the threat to stone them as a threat to revile them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r5.anchor: لنرجمنكم} : قال قتادة: بالحجارة. وقال مجاهد: بالشتم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p569#3/r6.claim: Their threatened painful punishment means a severe penalty.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r1.claim: تطيرنا means that they took the messengers as an ill omen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r1.anchor: تطيرنا بكم } تشاءمنا بكم ، وذلك أنهم كرهوا دينهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r2.claim: Ignorant people treat what they desire and accept as auspicious and what they dislike as ominous, attributing either good fortune or misfortune to it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r2.anchor: وعادة الجهال أن يتيمنوا بكل شيء مالوا إليه واشتهوه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r3.claim: The author compares their superstition with the Egyptians blaming Moses and his followers for misfortune.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r3.anchor: كما حكى الله عن القبط : { وإن تصبهم سيئة يطيروا بموسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r4.claim: He also compares it with Meccan polytheists who blamed the Prophet when misfortune befell them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r4.anchor: وعن مشركي مكة : { وإن تصبهم سيئة يقولوا هاذه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r5.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r5.claim: One view says drought and withheld rain prompted the people to call the messengers an ill omen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p11#3/r5.anchor: وقيل : حبس عنهم القطر فقالوا ذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r1.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r1.claim: They treated the messengers as a bad omen after misfortune; rain may have been withheld from Antioch.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r1.anchor: أحدها : تشاءمنا بكم , وعساهم قالوا ذلك لسوء أصابهم , قاله يحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r2.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r2.claim: Qatada says they blamed the messengers for harm, warning them not to leave their religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r2.anchor: الثاني : معناه إن أصابنا شر فإنما هو من أجلكم , قاله قتادة : تحذيرا من الرجوع عن دينهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r3.claim: It may also mean they felt aversion to the religion the messengers invited them to.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r3.anchor: استوحشنا منكم فيما دعوتمونا إليه من دينكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r4.claim: Qatada takes the threat as stoning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r6.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r6.claim: Al-Naqqash takes it as cursing and harming them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r7.claim: The painful punishment may be death.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p11/r8.claim: Alternatively, it may be painful torture before death.

MUQATIL:36:16-19/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r2.claim: They say they took the emissaries as ill omens because rain had been withheld and they blamed them for the drought.
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r2.anchor: يقول: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك أن المطر حبس عنهم، فقالوا: أصابنا هذا الشر يعنون قحط المطر من قبلكم

MUQATIL:36:16-19/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r3.claim: The threat means that if the messengers do not stop speaking, the townspeople will kill them by stoning.

MUQATIL:36:16-19/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r4.claim: The painful punishment threatened is a painful affliction.
MUQATIL:36:16-19/r4.anchor: { وليمسنكم } يعنى وليصيبنكم { منا عذاب أليم } [آية: 18] يعنى وجيعا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.claim: They call the messengers a bad omen because they dislike their religion; ignorant people treat what they like as auspicious and what they hate as unlucky.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r1.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم وذلك أنهم كرهوا دينهم ونفرت منه نفوسهم وعادة الجهال أن يتيمنوا بكل شىء مالوا إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.claim: Such people blame an unwanted event on ill fortune or credit a welcome event to a good omen.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r2.anchor: ويتشاءموا بما نفروا عنه وكرهوه فإن أصابهم بلاء أو نعمة قالوا بشؤم هذا وبركة ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.claim: Another explanation is that rain had been withheld, prompting their accusation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r3.anchor: وقيل حبس عنهم المطر فقالوا ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.claim: The threat to stone them can mean killing, expelling, or insulting them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ لنرجمنكم ﴾ لنقتلنكم أو لنطردنكم أو لنشتمنكم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.claim: The painful punishment threatened is the Fire, the most severe punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p6#3/r5.anchor: وليصيبنكم عذاب النار وهو أشد عذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r7.claim: The townspeople say they regarded the messengers as a bad omen.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r7.anchor: قالوا } لهم { إنا تطيرنا بكم } أي تشاءمنا بكم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r8.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r8.claim: Maqatil says rain was withheld from the town for three years, and the people blamed the messengers for the drought.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r8.anchor: قال مقاتل: حبس عنهم المطر ثلاث سنين فقالوا هذا بشؤمكم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r9.claim: Another account says the envoys spent ten years warning the people.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r9.anchor: ويقال: إنهم أقاموا ينذرونهم عشر سنين

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r10.claim: Al-Farra says “we will stone you” means “we will kill you”; he says most Quranic uses of rajm mean killing.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: لنقتلنكم. قال: وعامة ما في القرآن من الرجم معناه القتل

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r11.claim: Qatada understands the threat literally as stoning with rocks.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو على بابه من الرجم بالحجارة. وقيل: لنشتمنكم

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r12.claim: Another gloss is “we will insult you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r12.anchor: وقيل: لنشتمنكم وقد تقدم جميعه. { وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم }

QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r13.claim: The painful torment threatened may mean killing, painful punishment, or torment before killing—such as flaying, mutilation, or crucifixion.
QURTUBI-FULL:36:14-19/r13.anchor: قيل: هو القتل. وقيل: هو التعذيب المؤلم. وقيل: هو التعذيب المؤلم قبل القتل
